vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: boilerplates
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a placeholder for a boilerplate template collection based on a popular GitHub repository. The primary script, scripts/boilerplates.sh, contains only basic informational commands (help, info, status) and a 'TODO' placeholder for the main functionality, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or suspicious execution logic.

llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent and asks for no credentials or installs; it contains only a small, offline shell-wrapper and documentation, though its implementation is minimal compared to the description.

dimensions.detail: Name/description say it's a collection of boilerplate templates, but the package contains only documentation and a short shell script that prints help/info/status and has a TODO for 'run'. The requested permissions and resources (none) match the benign nature of the content, but the implementation is minimal and does not actually provide template-generation functionality as implied.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run simple commands (help/run/info/status). The included script does not read files, environment variables, or network resources. There is no instruction to access unrelated system files or exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is instruction-only with a small local shell script. Nothing is downloaded or written during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That aligns with its declared offline, no-API-keys usage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills/config. Autonomous invocation remains possible (platform default) but the skill's actions are limited and local.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears safe: it contains only docs and a tiny shell script that prints help/info/status and does not access network or secrets. However, its description promises a template collection but the implementation is essentially a stub—expect limited functionality. If you intend to use it as a template library, inspect or request the actual templates/source (the SKILL references ChristianLempa/boilerplates) before relying on it. As with any skill, review the included script before enabling autonomous invocation if you want to be absolutely cautious.
